description: A lot of us soften the truth because we're scared of how people will react, and then we call it love. God told Ezekiel not to be afraid of the nettles.
excerpt: We're supposed to speak truth. A lot of us soften it because we're scared of how people will react, and then we call that softening love. It's not love. It's fear.
verse: "Son of man, do not fear them or their words. Don't be afraid even though their threats surround you like nettles and briers and stinging scorpions."
body_html:
We're entering a time where this verse should speak to every one of us as Christians.

We're supposed to speak truth. A lot of us soften it because we're scared of how people will react, and then we call that softening love. It's not love. It's fear.

God knew Ezekiel would get pushback. He warned him right up front. And the picture He paints is pretty wild: nettles, briers, stinging scorpions. Not small annoyances. Things that sting on contact, catch your clothes and rip them, strike without warning.

That's what Ezekiel was walking into when he spoke truth. And it's what speaking truth looks like now too. People don't just politely disagree anymore. They come after your reputation, your job, your platform. The words sting. The reactions bite.

God doesn't tell Ezekiel it won't hurt. He tells him not to be afraid of it. Those are two different things. The pain is real, but fear isn't supposed to get the final say in what we speak.

I don't love this verse. I'd rather be liked than deal with nettles. But God isn't asking me to be comfortable. He's asking me to speak what's true, even when it leaves a mark on the people hearing it, and even when it leaves one on me.

Where have you been softening truth and calling it love, when God is actually asking you to speak it plainly?
question: Where have you been softening truth and calling it love, when God is actually asking you to speak it plainly?
